## Critique
- claim-1: Adequately grounded by [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]. This supplies both \(N\)-element generating families and the relevant meaning of minimality.
- claim-2: Correct. Generation induces \(\mathbb Z^N\twoheadrightarrow J/\Lambda_+J\). Under \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\), the representing square integral matrix is surjective, hence has determinant \(\pm1\). Thus the images form a basis, so no proper subfamily generates. The boundary \(N=1\), including \(a=0\) or \(b=0\), is covered.
- claim-3: Correct. Here \(A_+J=(2x^2,x^3)\); the degreewise quotient is \(\mathbb Z\) in degree \(1\), \(\mathbb Z/2\) in degree \(2\), and zero thereafter. Also \(x^2\notin(2x)\) and \(2x\notin(x^2)\), proving minimality. This explicitly refutes the converse implication.
